q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of thermoformed food containers?
title: Thermoformed container footprint per kg
short: Multiply the sheet used per kg of good containers, including skeleton waste, by your polymer's per-kg figure. Add sheet extrusion if done in house, the thermoformer's heaters, trimming and packing, then divide plant electricity by kg passed.
audience: Thermoformers making food trays, cups and clamshells

ul: PP, PET or PS sheet or resin by weight.
Skeleton waste reground and fed back, which cuts virgin input.
Sheet extrusion line, if you make your own sheet.
Thermoforming heaters and vacuum or pressure forming.

p: Give per kg and per piece with piece weight, since buyers compare by piece.

example.title: Worked example: thermoforming plant per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 63,900 / 100,000 = 0.639 kg CO2 per kg
Add polymer sheet or resin for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
